claims.quoted_text: the angles \(\angle BAP\) and \(\angle PAQ\) together form \(\angle BAC\)
claims.explanation: They form only 2θ of the five equal parts, not the whole angle BAC. Since ∠BAC=5θ, this statement is false; the equation ∠BAP+∠PAQ=2θ is true only as that partial sum.
In triangle APQ the interior angle at A is ∠PAQ=θ, not ∠BAP+∠PAQ=2θ. The correct sum is θ+x+y=180, so x=180−θ−y, not 180−2θ.
∠PAQ and ∠QAP are the same angle, so it is duplicated and ∠APQ is omitted. The correct triangle sum is θ+x+y=180, giving y=180−θ−x, not y=180−2θ.
This correspondence is not forced and is false. Different matches are possible; in the valid triangle, ∠BAC equals ∠AQP, while ∠APQ=θ+∠B, not 180−2θ.
∠BCA is the angle at C, not the sum of angles at A. The sum ∠QAR+∠RAS+∠SAC equals ∠QAC=3θ, so it is a portion of ∠BAC, not ∠BCA. Therefore C is not generally 3θ.
A negative number cannot equal a positive number. The computation after 1260−1440 gives −180/7, and flipping the sign is invalid.
The preceding computation gives 180°/7, not 36. The correct value of ∠B is 45/2=22.5°.
